items.note: A 167.5x147.7 pt square raster of a five-arrow cycle drawn as coloured ribbon-arrows around an open white centre that reads 'the Cycle of Food System' in three lines. The arrows run clockwise Production (red) - Processing (yellow) - Transport (grey) - Sale (purple) - Consumption/Waste (green), each carrying one inline clip-art glyph (a cow and sheaf, bottles, a truck and box, warehouse crates, a plate) and each name set along the arrow curve, so the two lower names print upside down. No axis, no number, no legend, no scale. Whole region is one image path, so no label exists in the text layer. Printed defect: the cycle closes on itself with no entry point and no stage is dated or quantified, so the diagram states the paper's scope and nothing else.

A 451.3x241.9 pt raster block diagram of the whole modelling chain: three source boxes (Plantation Source, Animal Husbandry Sources, Fishery Source) feeding a dark-blue 'Product Model', which splits into 'Product Probability', 'Food production' and 'Food Calories' and feeds a dark-blue 'Transport Model' beside a maroon circle 'Transportation Selection Algorithm'. Below, 'People Food Expenditure' and 'Food Demand' feed a dark-blue 'Sale Model' beside a maroon 'People Food Selection Algorithm', which yields 'Hungry People' and 'Sale Probability'. Grey arrows carry the two-model chain; thick red arrows carry the feedback into three yellow ellipses 'Sustainability', 'Equity' and 'Profitability', with an 'Optimized Model' box splitting into 'Excess', 'Benefit' and 'Cost'. No axis, no number, no legend for the two arrow colours. Printed defects: the 'Sustainability' ellipse clips its own label to 'Sustainabl' and 'Profitability' to 'Profitabilit' at the right edge, and the 'EW M' glyphs sit loose beside the red feedback arrow with no box.

note: Twenty-five pages, 72 measured regions: 25 page-foot WeChat stamps and 47 vector or raster clusters, of which 17 are exhibits and 30 are excluded with a note each - a clean partition with no duplicate exclusion. The exhibits are twelve numbered figures (1 to 12, no gaps) plus three real grids (Tables 1, 2 and 5), and two further exhibits numbered as tables but drawn as charts (Table 3 as two vertical bar charts, Table 4 as a 2x2 of grouped bar panels), so the census records 14 figure items and 3 tables. No exhibit is missing a measured region, so the paper declares no gap. The paper's real difficulty is the opposite of a gap: it is drawing-dense below the figures. Thirty regions look like extra exhibits and are not - thirteen display equations, two pseudocode algorithm boxes, six runs of prose whose inline maths clusters, two fragments of one braced equation group, two fragments of Table 1, one page of table of contents, and one Table 2 tail that crosses the page turn. Families: 3 flowchart-or-schematic (Figures 1, 2, 3, 5), 3 map-or-plan-view (4, 7, 8, all choropleths with no scale), 3 bar (6, plus Table 3 and Table 4), 2 line (10, 11), 1 scatter (12), 1 other (9, two radar charts) and 3 table-grid. Nine of the twelve figures are image-only, so no label exists in their text layer. Only one exhibit is ever cited twice (Table 1, then Table 4 and Figure 10); seven are never cited at all. The closing pages 23 to 25 carry no exhibit.
rules: Caption side is kind-driven on every row: all twelve figure captions print BELOW the exhibit and all three real tables print theirs ABOVE the grid - Table 1 y460.8 over a head starting at 493.1, Table 2 y666.3 over 680.8, Table 5 y122.8 over 137.3 - while the two exhibits this paper NUMBERS as tables and draws as charts print their caption above as well (Table 3 y328.8 over 347.8, Table 4 y546.5 over 567.0), so [caption.position] is 'above' on all five numbered tables and 'below' on all twelve figures.

The printed number does not name the drawing twice: Tables 3 and 4 carry a 'Table N' caption over what is drawn as, respectively, two vertical bar charts of net calorie input and a 2x2 of grouped before/after bar panels. Both are recorded as figure items with the family of the drawing and the numbering of the caption ('Table N'), because this lane counts what is drawn (README: 'what charts are actually drawn in these papers, not what the captions say'), which is why [caption.numbering] carries 'Table N' on those two rows while [geometry.family] carries the drawn type; only Tables 1, 2 and 5 are grids and live in the tables list.

Every caption is a single title sentence that names an exhibit and stops - not one states a unit, a variable list or any reading of what the exhibit shows - so [caption.words] runs 4 to 13 across the fifteen rows and only Table 4's caption reaches 13, which is the paper's whole caption vocabulary.

Three caption lines print in a different style from the rest and are quoted as printed: Table 2 has NO colon ('Table 2 Calories and ratios of different types of food'), Figure 12 prints a space before its colon ('Figure 12 : Diagram of cost and benefit optimization in multiple countries'), and Figures 3, 5 and 11 are glued to the preceding prose in the text layer ('as shown in Figure 3.', 'els Figure 5: Transportation flow chart', '29th months respectively. Figure 11: Change curve of cost and benefit'), so those three [caption.verbatim] values are cut out of the raw line rather than read as a standalone line.

The twelve charts are drawn as twelve separate embedded rasters, one image path each, and the paper's printed numbering runs 1 to 12 with no gap; the eight vector exhibits that look like extra charts are all display equations, symbol lists or pseudocode and every one is excluded with its own note, so [geometry.family] is never taken from a crop that holds only maths.

Multi-panel exhibits keep the family of their panels and carry [geometry.panel_count]: Figures 4, 7, 8, 9 and Table 3 hold two panels each, Table 4 holds four in a 2x2 frame, and no exhibit in the paper is composite-panel, because no multi-panel frame here mixes families.

The map-or-plan-view family takes three exhibits (Figures 4, 7 and 8), all four-shade choropleths of India, France or Japan; none carries a scale bar, a numeric class break or a colourbar, so [geometry.colorbar] is false and [geometry.printed_numbers] is false on all three.

The flowchart-or-schematic family takes four exhibits (Figures 1, 2, 3 and 5), all clip-art schematics with no axis and no quantity, so [geometry.printed_numbers] is false and the [geometry.legend] key is 'none' on all four; Figure 2 is the only diagram in the paper that uses colour to carry meaning (grey chain versus red feedback) and prints no key for it.

Section assignment follows the nearest preceding printed heading: F1 1.1, F2 1.3, Table 1 under '3 Notations', F3 4.1, Table 2 4.2, F4 5.1, F5 5.2, F6 and F7 8.1.1, Table 3 8.1.2, F8 8.1.3, and Table 4, F9, Table 5, F10, F11 and F12 all under 8.2.2 'Optimized result' - the paper's results section holds ten of the seventeen exhibits - every one keyed by its [place.section_path].

Citations are sparse and mostly lower-case: ten of the seventeen exhibits carry a pointer and seven are never cited (Figures 1, 2, 4 and 5, Tables 2 and 5, and Figure 3's only 'pointer' is the caption itself). The pointers use four spellings - 'Figure N', 'figure N', 'Table N' and 'table N' - so [mention.style] carries the spelling actually printed on each row, and Table 1's two citations sit four pages apart, on p6 and p8.

Two exhibits recite a value the drawing cannot show: Table 4 is read on p20 for a land-area change and a water drop 'from 5.762 billion per month', and Figure 10 is read on p21 for month 37 and month 43, both of which print as bare callout coordinates ('X:43 Y:96.92') rather than as an axis value; both rows carry [mention.count] 2 against a drawing that cannot show either number.

Printed defects are recorded per row: the in-figure titles of Figure 9 misspell 'Changes' as 'Chages' and Table 4 titles its third panel 'Water Consumes', Table 5 calls the two countries 'counties', Figure 6's India bar stops near 63 percent on a 100 percent axis, Table 3's y axis omits every other labelled step and its district names collide, Figure 11 crams its x ticks into one unreadable string, and Figure 12 inverts its vertical axis so 0 sits at the top, which is why [geometry.printed_numbers] is false on the last of those and true on the rest.
